Effective dose from cosmic radiation, estimated from flight time and route
Explain how cosmic radiation is calculated

The effective dose from cosmic radiation in millisieverts (mSv) - the radiation the body is exposed to at cruising altitude. The tile shows the current year, the detail page lists every year. It is an estimate from the logbook data, not a measurement.

Dose = dose rate × flight time. The dose rate at cruising altitude increases with altitude and with geographic latitude: 3 µSv/h at 10 km × e^(0.35 × (altitude − 10 km)) × (1 + sin² latitude). It is lowest at the equator and about twice as high at the poles. Units: 1 mSv = 1,000 µSv.

Flight time and route come from the logbook entry; if the flight time is missing, it is estimated from the route (805 km/h plus 25 minutes). The route is the great-circle distance between the app\'s airport coordinates. The cruising altitude is estimated from the distance: 9 km on short-haul up to 12 km on long-haul. The latitude is that of the great-circle midpoint. Ground transfers do not count.

German Federal Office for Radiation Protection (BfS), “Cosmic radiation and flying”: at ground level about 300 µSv per year, at 11 km altitude north of the 60th parallel 8–9 µSv per hour, Frankfurt–New York round trip about 120 µSv. FED aviation standard: 4 µSv/h at 10 km altitude. The typical annual dose of flight crew is 2–6 mSv.

It is an estimate, not a measurement. Not modeled are: solar activity (it varies the dose by about 15–30 %), the aircraft\'s actual cruising altitude, and the approximation of geomagnetic latitude by geographic latitude. Individual flights can therefore deviate upwards or downwards.

The estimated effective dose from cosmic radiation for this year is above 20 mSv. That is the upper limit for the annual radiation exposure of flying personnel (occupationally exposed persons, category A of the German Radiation Protection Ordinance). This figure is an estimate from flight time and route, not a measurement - the calculation is explained via the i at the top right of the detail page.

Great that you\'re using Logbook!\n\nIn this tour I\'ll walk you through a few settings step by step and show you the basics.
Tap to pick an icon or photo
The dashboard sums up your logbook in tiles – flights, distance, time, countries and more.
Filter by flight type and period
Above the tiles you choose whether duty, private or all flights are counted and for which period.
A tap opens a tile\'s details. A long press lets you move the tiles around.
Under “Entries” you collect all your flights – chronological and searchable.
Use the plus button to create a flight: route, date, airline, flight type and optionally more.
Tap an entry to edit or delete it. The magnifier searches your logbook.
Two pages reward your curiosity: Discovery and the scratch map.
Shows the routes you flew for the first time in a given year.
Colours in every country you visited and shows your progress around the world.
